readerMoment: Has written the lab scope and mapped their own subnet and router. Has used a terminal, but does not know which services on their own machine wait for network traffic.
outcome: Can list TCP listeners and UDP sockets on one machine they own, then record each local address, port, process, likely reach, and purpose without changing any service.
coreModel: A loopback-bound service cannot be reached directly from another device, while a wildcard or LAN-bound service may be reachable if the network and firewall allow it.

prerequisites.idea: Which machine and traffic are in scope

teachingShape.realTask: Make a read-only listener inventory of one machine you own
activate: Recall the machine's own IP and subnet from the previous page
A door has both a room number (port) and an entrance (bind address)
demonstrate: One annotated sample output: loopback TCP, wildcard TCP, and UDP with process names
One completed inventory with cautious reach and purpose, including an unknown
apply: Run the inspection commands for the reader's OS on one owned machine
Record two of their own results, checking unknown processes before making any changes
integrate: Use the inventory as input to the dated baseline on the next page

requiredIdeas: A process owns a socket with a local address and port; TCP LISTEN waits for connections, while UDP sockets do not have a LISTEN state.
127.0.0.1 and ::1 are loopback; 0.0.0.0 and :: mean all available interfaces for that address family; a specific LAN address binds that interface.
A bind address suggests possible reach, not proof of access: host firewall, routing, and interface state also matter.
Commands inspect locally; elevation may be needed to see process ownership. Never change or stop an unknown service from an inventory alone.
Record protocol, bind address, port, process, possible reach, purpose, and any uncertainty without posting real host details.
candidateAnalogies: A door number is a port; the entrance it faces is the bind address. A locked hallway (firewall) can still prevent entry.
visualNeeds: Three labeled entrances on one owned host: loopback, a specific LAN address, and all interfaces, with external reach marked as conditional

deliberatelyExcluded.why: This page inspects only the owned host; consent and network reach are separate questions.
First record what exists; firewall policy and changes belong to later pages.
Owned by the following inventory page.

nextPagePressure: A single host inventory becomes useful when the reader dates it, repeats it, and compares it with other owned devices.
